title: One record per kind
environment: Data files written into a fresh folder, then loaded through the store.
records: One small Tool Library product (TL) with a record of every kind, a row of every part table, a link of every relation, and the declaration and checking rows.
prepare: A test calls everyKind(), changes the rows it needs (withTable), and writes them with writeData() or loads them through the store.
reset: removeData() in afterAll removes every folder writeData() made.
description: The store's and the writers' starting data: every table holds rows that load, so a test changes one thing and reads what the store accepts or refuses.

title: Complete example library
environment: A fresh product folder, written through the store's command layer with the code files its records name, then loaded with Lathe's built-in checks.
records: Product EX (Example library) with one domain, EX-LEND, and a record of nearly every kind, every obligation designed, built and proved: no problem and no gap.
prepare: A test builds complete() with build() or loadData(), often after adding, removing or changing rows (adding, without, changing) or leaving out code files.
reset: removeData() in afterAll removes the folders.
description: The engine's baseline product: a test breaks one thing in it and expects exactly the problem or gap that follows.

title: Fresh flow product repo
environment: A fresh product repo with lathe.config.json and data/, with the real `lathe` command run on it as a child process.
records: Product TL (Tool Library) only; a flow seeds what its use case assumes through the store, such as LENDING: the Lending domain with a Loan aggregate, its root entity and a field, Open a loan and Loan opened, a capability, Borrow a tool and one UC requirement.
prepare: product() makes the repo; the flow test calls seed() with the commands it starts from, then walks its steps through the command.
reset: removeProducts() in afterAll removes every repo the file made.
description: The flow tests' product: each flow runs the way the Owner or an Agent would, through the command line.

title: A product with its declarations
environment: An empty product repo (lathe.config.json and an empty data folder), loaded through the store.
records: Product TL (Tool Library) with roles Member and Librarian, interface TL-IF01 (web app), open question TL-Q01 owned by the Librarian, product kind report under the product with fields file and usage, and product relation measured_by from business_outcome to report.
prepare: productDataSet(store) runs Add a product, Add an interface, Add an open question, Declare a product kind and Declare a product relation, in order.
reset: Each test writes a fresh folder; its stores are closed after it.
description: The Product aggregate's own records, built only with its own Add commands.

title: Two business outcomes
environment: Data files written into a fresh folder, then loaded through the store.
records: Product TL with domain TL-LEND, capability TL-LEND-CAP01 and a domain service test TL-LEND-DS01-T01; then outcomes TL-BO01, measured by that test, and TL-BO02, measured outside the code.
prepare: businessOutcomeDataSet() writes the base rows and runs Add a business outcome twice.
reset: Each test writes a fresh folder; its stores are closed after it.
description: The Business outcome aggregate's records, built with its own Add command on the least other aggregates must give.

title: Extension record records
environment: Data files written into a fresh folder, then loaded through the store.
records: Products TL and OT with domains TL-LEND and OT-D; TL-LEND with an aggregate, entity and command; TL's product kinds report (under a domain) and report_section (under a report) and relation reports_on; then report TL-LEND-RP01 with its link and package, and section TL-LEND-RP01-S01.
prepare: extensionRecordDataSet() writes the base rows and runs Add an extension record for each record.
reset: Each test writes a fresh folder; its stores are closed after it.
description: The Extension record aggregate's records, built with its own Add command under declarations written as data.

title: Two entry points
environment: Data files written into a fresh folder, then loaded through the store.
records: Product TL with a role, domain TL-LEND and standard rule TL-STD-CODE-R01; then entry points TL-LEND-ENTRY01 (using vitest, meeting the rule) and TL-LEND-ENTRY02.
prepare: entryPointDataSet() writes the base rows and runs Add an entry point twice.
reset: Each test writes a fresh folder; its stores are closed after it.
description: The Entry point aggregate's records, built with its own Add command.

title: Two tooling records
environment: Data files written into a fresh folder, then loaded through the store.
records: Product TL with a role, domain TL-LEND and standard rule TL-STD-CODE-R01; then tooling records TL-LEND-TOOL01 (using vitest, meeting the rule) and TL-LEND-TOOL02.
prepare: toolingDataSet() writes the base rows and runs Add a tooling record twice.
reset: Each test writes a fresh folder; its stores are closed after it.
description: The Tooling aggregate's records, built with its own Add command.

title: Component-test products
environment: jsdom in Vitest: each data folder is loaded through the store once per run by the global setup, and the app reads it through a stubbed fetch of GET /api/spec.
records: Five data folders: workspace (products DM, Demo shop, with two domains, and NF, Notebook), model (product P with a whole domain model in P-D and P-E), patterns, product-kinds and standards, each with the problems and coverage the engine would find.
prepare: openApp() or serve() serves the workspace fixture unless the test passes another; fixture() hands a fresh copy, which a test may change with addRows().
reset: Nothing to reset: each test gets a fresh copy of the rows, and the next openApp() cleans up the page.
description: What the app's component tests read: small products shaped for the pages, the graph and the ERD stage.

title: Lathe's spec, served
environment: The app's Vite dev server on a free local port (never 5199), over a copy of this repo's data/ and lathe.config.json in a fresh folder; Playwright drives Chromium with one worker.
records: Lathe's own specification, product LA, as it stands when the suite starts (about 5,000 rows).
prepare: The Playwright config copies the data and starts the server once for the stability and accessibility suites; a scenario that writes calls keepData() first.
reset: The function keepData() returns puts every data file back and removes any the scenario added; the global teardown removes the copy.
description: The stability and accessibility suites' product: the real spec in the real app, so layout, focus and audits are measured on real pages.

title: This repo's own specifications
environment: The data folders as checked in, read through the store in place.
records: Lathe's own specification (product LA, data/) and the Tool Library's (product TL, examples/tool-library/data/).
prepare: A test loads data/ or examples/tool-library/ with the store or loadWorkspace; nothing is written.
reset: Nothing to reset: the tests only read.
description: The real products as data: tests that every real record loads, is drawn readably and holds to its own checks.

title: Lathe's spec, production build
environment: The app built for production and served with `lathe serve`'s server on a free local port (never 5199), over a copy of this repo's data/ and lathe.config.json; Playwright drives Chromium with one worker.
records: Lathe's own specification, product LA (about 5,000 rows).
prepare: The perf Playwright config copies the data; perf/serve.ts builds the app and serves it.
reset: The global teardown removes the copy of the data and the build.
description: The app's performance budgets, measured on what a product's `lathe serve` and the desktop app ship.

title: Lathe's spec times seven
environment: A copy of this repo's data and config in a fresh folder, with the code folders linked so tests' files resolve; and a synthetic product in another fresh folder.
records: Lathe's own specification, product LA; and Lathe's data six times over under the prefixes LB to LG, about 10,000 records, without LA's own checks and kinds.
prepare: lathe/perf/engine.ts makes both folders before it measures.
reset: The script removes both folders when it is done.
description: The engine's performance budgets: a cold load and a live reload of the real spec, and a load of a product about twice its size, measured without a budget.

title: One-domain desktop shop
environment: The real Electron shell, hidden, on a product folder in a fresh folder, after the engine and app build and the desktop build.
records: Product SMK (Smoke Shop) with one domain, SMK-ORD (Orders).
prepare: beforeAll builds Lathe if its build is stale, builds the shell, turns off macOS window restoration and writes the product's config and data files.
reset: afterAll stops every Electron the file started and removes the folder.
description: The desktop smoke test's product: just enough for a window to open it, serve it and run its menus.

title: Every minimum missed
environment: A fresh product folder, written through the store's command layer, then loaded with Lathe's built-in checks.
records: Product SP (Sparse) with two domains (SP-D and an empty SP-E) and one record short of every minimum that coverage reports, such as an outcome no capability serves.
prepare: A test builds sparse() with build() or loadData().
reset: removeData() in afterAll removes the folders.
description: Coverage's gaps, one of each: a test expects every gap the product falls short by, and the command line's report of them.
